data.exact_reserve_text: As at the 31 December 2020, the 2018 underwriting year was reinsured to close ("RITC") externally resulting in the Syndicate having only transactions relating to 2019 to 2021 underwriting years during the 2021 financial year.

prior_year_events.impact_description: 2018 underwriting year was reinsured to close externally, reducing gross claims outstanding recorded on the Syndicate.

data.standardized_narrative: Opening gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2021 was GBP 58.723m and closing gross claims outstanding at 31 December 2021 was GBP 65.471m. Prior-year development excluding current year movements is effectively flat based on the gross claims development table (no net movement identified). The reported movements include a material RITC of closed years which reduced gross reserves by GBP 14.403m and other current-year claim activity increased the overall gross reserves. No quantified adverse or favourable prior-year development (net) is reported in gross terms.
raw_causal_phrases: As at the 31 December 2020, the 2018 underwriting year was reinsured to close ("RITC") externally resulting in the Syndicate having only transactions relating to 2019 to 2021 underwriting years during the 2021 financial year.
Claims incurred in the prior accident years
data.data_quality_notes: No explicit single-line 'movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding' gross figure was provided. Prior-year development was derived from the gross claims development triangle (gross) which shows no net movement for the older underwriting years (2019 and earlier columns available). The claims outstanding reconciliation includes 'Claims incurred in the prior accident years' (GBP 0.764m) and a substantial 'RITC of closed years' (-GBP 14.403m) which is a reinsurance-to-close transaction that materially reduces gross reserves; care was taken to treat RITC as a transfer rather than pure prior-year development. If a report-level gross prior-year movement figure is required, none is explicitly stated; the triangle-based result (0.0) was used.
